description: The flow operator ->>: statements chain left to right, a stage reads a PRIOR stage's result via a $n table reference (n counts backward - $1 is the immediately preceding statement, equivalent to consuming its RESULT_SCAN), and the chain's result is the LAST statement's result. SHOW results chain through SELECTs, DML row counts flow through, an out-of-range $n fails as the unresolvable generated name SQL_PIPE_n at 'error line 0 at position -1', a $n with no chain at all is an 'invalid pipe reference' at its real position, and ordinary positional $n references (VALUES + ORDER BY $1) are unaffected. Converted from features/FlowOperatorTest; its two multi-result-set introspection asserts (a chain yields ONE result set, a plain script two) stay in the trimmed Java class.

steps.sql:
show tables
->> select "name" from $1
->> select * from $1
select 1 as a ->> select 2 as b ->> select * from $2
